head: Pakistan joined its Indus river dolphin sanctuaries into one 400-kilometre protected corridor.
summary: The Punjnad Indus River Dolphin Sanctuary, created in June 2026, protects nearly 200 kilometres of river in Punjab and connects with existing reserves in Sindh. A 2025 study estimated 1,987 dolphins, up from 617 in 2001, with 99 percent living in a 690-kilometre stretch between the Chashma and Sukkur barrages. Gillnets caused 52 percent of documented deaths from 2008 to 2023, and they remain the main threat the new protections must address.

head: Asháninka fire brigades brought wildfires in 45 Peruvian communities down to zero.
summary: Across 45 Asháninka communities in Peru's Ene River region, wildfires fell from 25 in 2023 to nine in 2024, and none were recorded in 2025. Community members trained as certified firefighters watch for smoke by satellite, drone and radio under the Paamari programme, run by the Central Asháninka of the Ene River with the charity Cool Earth. Burned area dropped from 2,648 hectares to 492 in a year when fires across Peru destroyed 63,000 hectares.

head: A bird unseen for thirteen years reappeared in an Ivorian rainforest.
summary: Field researchers photographed a Ghana cuckooshrike in Côte d'Ivoire's Taï National Park in June, the species' first confirmed sighting since 2013. Stephanie Bartlett and Paulo Ditzel of the International Bird Conservation Partnership spent six months surveying West Africa's forests before capturing what may be the best photographs ever taken of the bird. The team plans to return to Taï within the year to survey further and strengthen ties with the local researchers protecting the park's shrinking forest.

head: Pakistan linked two river reserves into a single 400-kilometer sanctuary for the world's rarest dolphin.
summary: The government's new Punjnad Indus River Dolphin Sanctuary now connects with an existing reserve in Sindh, giving the critically endangered, functionally blind species a continuous protected corridor along the river. A 2025 survey counted roughly 1,987 of the dolphins, up from a low of 617 in 2001, though gillnets still cause more than half of recorded deaths. WWF-Pakistan biologist Uzma Khan says the connected corridor lets dolphins move between feeding grounds without crossing the busiest fishing waters.

head: Genetic testing revealed a fourth gentoo penguin species hiding on a remote sub-Antarctic island.
summary: An international team analyzing genomes, body size, calls, and breeding schedules confirmed that gentoo penguins on France's remote Kerguelen Islands form their own species, Pygoscelis kerguelensis — the first new penguin species named in more than a century. The researchers, publishing in Communications Biology, found that three populations long treated as mere subspecies are genetically distinct enough to split the familiar gentoo penguin into four separate species. Conservationists say the finer-grained map gives each population, several already vulnerable to warming seas, a clearer claim to its own protection.

head: A tropical heat pool sent 695 billion tons of extra snow onto East Antarctica.
summary: Between 2021 and 2023, satellites recorded East Antarctica's largest ice-mass gain on record, equal to about four years of the continent's average annual loss. Researcher Qinghua Ding traced the cause to unusual warming in the tropical Pacific-Indian "warm pool," which sent an atmospheric river of moisture toward Queen Mary Land and Wilkes Land as heavy snow. Only 9 percent of the anomaly was linked to human-caused warming, and researchers say the gain is temporary, not a reversal of the ice sheet's long-term decline.

head: Wildlife officers built a fifty-foot tunnel so rare possums could find mates across a highway.
summary: Victoria's Great Alpine Road cuts straight through the range of the mountain pygmy-possum at Little Mount Higginbotham, splitting a population of roughly 150 four-inch marsupials from mates on the other side. The Department of Environment, Land, Water and Planning built a nearly 50-foot underpass beneath the road, and over two summers 30 possums used it, crossing in about 15 seconds each, while Zoos Victoria's Healesville Sanctuary tracked hibernation by thermal camera. Fewer than 2,000 of the possums are left in the wild, and the sanctuary recorded 12 joeys born this past March — a sign the tunnel is doing its job.

head: Six Irrawaddy dolphin calves were born in the Mekong this year.
summary: Five calves surfaced in Cambodia's Kratie province and one in neighboring Stung Treng, lifting the river's known population of the endangered dolphins to about 118. Seventy-two river guards now patrol 180 kilometers of protected habitat, working with WWF-Cambodia to curb the illegal gillnets and electrofishing that helped cut the population from roughly 200 in the late 1990s. The dolphins have already vanished from the Mekong Delta and Tonle Sap Lake, so each calf gives the fishing communities whose tourism depends on them one more reason to keep the patrols funded.

head: Two reintroduced beavers raised a Cheshire peatland's groundwater nearly forty-fold.
summary: Ecologist Melanie Baker's four-year study found that two Eurasian beavers, released into a fenced 4.5-hectare enclosure at Hatch Mere in Cheshire, raised local groundwater levels by up to 37 times and lifted surface water by a median of 50 centimeters. Working with the Cheshire Wildlife Trust, the beavers built dams that kept the peatland measurably wetter through the dry summer of 2022 than the surrounding land. Baker says the findings point to beavers as a low-cost way to make Britain's drained peat bogs more resilient to drought.

head: A giant anteater turned up in an Argentine reserve that hadn't seen one in forty years.
summary: A male giant anteater was spotted last year at the Alma Guaraní Natural Reserve in Argentina's Corrientes province, the region's first recorded sighting of the species since 1986. Researcher Rosario Montiel of the National University of the Northeast called the appearance "the first register of the giant anteater in 40 years in Corrientes province, and it was spontaneous," arriving after four years of restoration work returned ecological function to more than 150 of the reserve's 6,400 hectares, with native trees replanted on eleven more. Montiel's team now hopes to bring in female anteaters to keep the newcomer company, though roaming dogs and fragmented farmland still make it hard for the animals to move between forest patches.
